full_judgment:
7. The Leave Petition was heard by the full Bench and after hearing discharged the Rule as being infructuous. In the meantime the respondent No. 3 again recommended the application of the respondent No. 7 Samity instead of recommending the petitioner, observing that there is no scope for considering the application of the petitioner. It is stated that on 13-4-2021 the authority concern vide memo No. 31.00.0000.050.68.013.21.308 took decision to collect khas collection of revenue till lease process is exhausted. 

 17. District Jolmohal Management Committee in its meeting dated 1-6-2021, having considered all those five applications afresh, recommended this respondent to lease out the Nodi in question under development scheme for 1428-1433 BS to the Ministry of Land. The petitioner, challenging the aforesaid decision of the District Jolmohal Management Committee filed Writ Petition No. 5320 of 2021 before this Court and obtained a Rule along with an interim order of status-quo. The respondent No. 7, filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1700 of 2021, before the Honorable Appellate Division and on 2-9-2021 the Honorable Judge-in-Chamber, after hearing modified the order directing the parties to maintain status-quo in respect of possession and position of the Jalmahal in question till hearing of the civil petition for leave to appeal. However, the government-respondent Nos. 1-6 are at liberty to collect revenue from the fishery in question through khas collection. Thereafter, the CPLA was disposed of on 26-9-2021 with observation to dispose of the Writ Petition by the High Court Division expeditiously maintaining the order dated 2-9-2021.
